problem_statement.body:
On static analysis specify to Scrapy projects, at the moment there only seems to be https://github.com/stummjr/flake8-scrapy

I think we should come up with additional checks based on our day-to-day experiences using Scrapy and common issues we see in the community, specially in new users, and implement them in https://github.com/stummjr/flake8-scrapy (or a fork if needed) when possible, and look for alternatives in case of checks that cannot be implemented that way.

problem_statement.title: running materialized_view always results in a full rebuild
problem_statement.body:
### Describe the bug
Re-running a materialized view always recreates the view, rather than triggering a refresh.

### Steps To Reproduce
1. Create a materialized_view
2. Run it
3. Run it again and watch it get recreated

### Expected behavior
After the first run, subsequent runs (assuming there are no changes to the model or config) will trigger a refresh of the view, not a rebuild.

### System information
**The output of `dbt --version`:**
```
Core:
  - installed: 1.11.2
  - latest:    1.11.2 - Up to date!

Plugins:
  - spark:      1.10.0 - Up to date!
  - databricks: 1.11.4 - Up to date!
```

**The operating system you're using:**
Linux

**The output of `python --version`:**
Python 3.13.11

### Additional context
Digging around the code, this is being caused by the huge number of tblproperties that Databricks is automatically applying to the materialized view. Although there is a list of properties to ignore, it only covers a small subset of the properties that Databricks is applying. Trying to manage this via a hardcoded list of properties is going to be a losing battle, as they are constantly adding new ones.

title: Handle oversized chunks for variables along unlimited dimensions
issue_title: unlimited dims may cause the chunksize to exceed the shape

gold_patch:
diff --git a/docs/releases.md b/docs/releases.md
index c63829b94..ff0ce2a34 100644
--- a/docs/releases.md
+++ b/docs/releases.md
@@ -11,6 +11,11 @@
 - `open_virtual_dataset` and `open_virtual_datatree` now populate `ds.encoding["source"]` with the normalized source URI, mirroring [`xarray.open_dataset`][]'s behaviour. Parsers that have already set `encoding["source"]` are left untouched.
   By [Tom Nicholas](https://github.com/TomNicholas).
 
+### Bug fixes
+
+- Handle chunk shapes larger than the array shape for variables along an unlimited dimension. HDF5 allocates a chunk sized for the full (unlimited) `maxshape` — e.g. a coordinate holding 5 values reports `chunks=(512,)` — which inhibited concatenation of the resulting virtual dataset. The `HDFParser` now trims the chunk shape down to the array shape (adjusting the manifest byte ranges accordingly) when it is safe to do so, i.e. the chunk is uncompressed and only its leading dimension is oversized. When trimming isn't possible (e.g. a compressed coordinate, as in the ERA5 archive), the variable is left untrimmed — it still reads and writes as virtual references correctly — and `to_virtual_dataset` now emits a warning naming the affected variable(s) and suggesting they be passed to `loadable_variables` so the dataset can be concatenated. Closes [#803](https://github.com/zarr-developers/VirtualiZarr/issues/803).
+  By [Tom Nicholas](https://github.com/TomNicholas).
+
 ### Documentation
 
 - Document that virtual concatenation also requires homogeneous CF encoding (`scale_factor`/`add_offset`) across files — xarray's default attribute-merging silently drops mismatched values and produces incorrectly-decoded data on read. Added a new FAQ bullet and a warning admonition under "Combining virtual datasets" in the usage docs. See [#1004](https://github.com/zarr-developers/VirtualiZarr/issues/1004).

+def _warn_about_oversized_virtual_chunks(vds: "xr.Dataset") -> None:
+    """
+    Warn if any still-virtual variable has a chunk larger than its array shape.
+
+    Such chunks arise for variables along an unlimited dimension whose oversized
+    chunk could not be trimmed (e.g. because it is compressed). They read and
+    write as virtual references fine, but cannot be concatenated with other
+    virtual datasets - the oversized final chunk prevents forming a regular
+    chunk grid - so point the user at loading them instead. Variables that were
+    loaded (no longer backed by a ManifestArray) are unaffected and not warned
+    about.
+    """
+    oversized = [
+        name

problem_statement.title: unlimited dims may cause the chunksize to exceed the shape
problem_statement.body:
When opening a dataset with a coordinate along a unlimited dim the chunksize may be larger than the shape if we don't load the values of the variable into memory:

```python
import netCDF4

with netCDF4.Dataset("test.nc", mode="w") as f:
    dim_time = f.createDimension("time", None)
    var_time = f.createVariable("time", "i8", ("time",))
    var_time[:5] = 10

import virtualizarr

import xarray as xr
from obstore.store import LocalStore

from virtualizarr import open_virtual_dataset, open_virtual_mfdataset
from virtualizarr.parsers import HDFParser
from virtualizarr.registry import ObjectStoreRegistry

from pathlib import Path

store_path = Path.cwd()
file_path = str(store_path / "test.nc")
file_url = f"file://{file_path}"

store = LocalStore(prefix=store_path)
registry = ObjectStoreRegistry({file_url: store})

parser = HDFParser()
vds = open_virtual_dataset(
  url=file_url,
  parser=parser,
  registry=registry,
  loadable_variables=[],
)

vds["time"].data
```

This currently prints as
```
ManifestArray<shape=(5,), dtype=int64, chunks=(512,)>
```

The chunk shape comes from `h5py`:
```python
import h5py

with h5py.File("test.nc", mode="r") as f:
    print(f["time"].shape, f["time"].maxshape, f["time"].chunks)
```

This is a problem because it inhibits concatenation of virtual datasets or loading written (zarrquet) files.

title: fix(tooling): honour diag-fields-exempt for unresolvable fields in all 3 passes
issue_title: Diagnostic-fields gate: the `# diag-fields-exempt` opt-out is honoured by only one of three passes
gold_patch:
diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index 0ce9f8650..d137451b8 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -13,6 +13,7 @@ The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).
 
 ### Fixed
 
+- **`check_diagnostic_fields.py`'s `# diag-fields-exempt` opt-out is now honoured wherever an *unresolvable* field can arise** ([#955](https://github.com/aallan/vera/issues/955)).  The field-presence pass (`check_source`) appended its non-literal-severity violation and `continue`d **before** its own opt-out lookup ran, so a marker on that exact call was never consulted even in the one pass that otherwise honours it; the `spec_ref`-validity pass never consulted the opt-out at all.  Fixed for the *unresolvable* (non-literal) sub-case only: a non-literal severity or spec_ref can't be checked statically and so is opt-out-able, same as a missing field — with the marker found anywhere across a multi-line call's span, not just the argument's own line.  A `spec_ref` that resolves but cites the wrong/nonexistent section, or an `error_code` not in `ERROR_CODES`, is a content error, not a tagging gap — the opt-out never suppresses either, marker or not; and the `error_code` pass skips non-literal codes entirely, so it has nothing to waive.  On `vera/` the exempt set is unaffected (the three existing real markers are all missing-field cases).  `main()`'s remedy text now states this precisely instead of implying the opt-out waives everything it lists.  External contribution by [@chethanuk](https://github.com/chethanuk).
 - **The diagnostic-fields gate's plumbing-skip now also confirms the sole own-scope `Diagnostic` is reachable as the helper's *result*** ([#956](https://github.com/aallan/vera/issues/956)).  The `#827` narrowing (v0.1.1) requires a genuine helper method whose sole own-scope construction is ambiguity-free, but never checked that the construction was actually *used* as the helper's output — a helper that builds its one `Diagnostic` and hands it to something other than a `return` / `.append(...)` (e.g. `self.dispatch(d)`) still had that ctor elected as plumbing and skipped by all three passes, so a bogus `spec_ref` or unregistered `error_code` on it would ship silently.  A new `_ctor_is_reachable_as_result` predicate now requires the ctor be return-ed, appended, or bound to a local later return-ed/appended, gated after the existing `len(ctors) == 1` check so the `#827` ambiguity handling is untouched.  The name-based return/append match has no real data-flow, so a local rebound after the ctor-binding assign — plain reassignment (`d = Diagnostic(...)`; `d = something_else`; `return d`), a `for`/`with` loop target, a walrus, an augmented assignment, or an `except ... as` name — would otherwise still match on the name and be wrongly treated as reachable — fixed by counting binding sites *generically* rather than by enumerating statement forms (every Store-context name — assignment or unpack of any shape, `for`/`with` targets, walrus — plus `import ... as`, `except ... as`, `match` captures, the helper's own parameters, and `nonlocal` declarations in nested functions; a bare annotation carries no assignment and is not counted): a name bound more than once anywhere in own scope is treated as unreliable rather than reachable, and the return/append name-match only counts at-or-after the binding line.  Separately, `_is_append_call` treated ANY `.append(...)` call as evidence of reachability, including an append to an unrelated throwaway local (`tmp = []; tmp.append(d)`) that the helper never reads again — every real diagnostic-list sink in `vera/` has the `self.<attr>.append(...)` shape, so the check is now scoped to that.  On `vera/` the exempt set is unchanged (all five real helpers return or append their sole ctor directly), so nothing new is flagged in the live tree — the gap was latent, closed defensively.  External contribution by [@chethanuk](https://github.com/chethanuk).

problem_statement.title: Diagnostic-fields gate: the `# diag-fields-exempt` opt-out is honoured by only one of three passes
problem_statement.body:
## Summary

`scripts/check_diagnostic_fields.py` tells authors to silence a violation with
`# diag-fields-exempt: <reason>`, but only **one** of its three passes actually
honours that marker.

The failure report (`main()`, near the "Populate the missing field(s) / fix the
spec_ref / register the error_code, or add `# diag-fields-exempt: <reason>` for a
genuinely ..." line) advertises the opt-out as the remedy for *every* violation
class. `_optout_lines()` is consulted only in `check_source()` (the field-presence
pass). Neither `_iter_spec_refs()` (spec_ref validity) nor
`_diagnostic_call_sites()` (error_code registration) reads it.

## Reproduction

```python
# vera/checker/x.py
REF = 'Chapter 4, Section 4.3 "Slot References"'
def check(node):
    return Diagnostic(description='d', rationale='r', fix='f',
                      spec_ref=REF)  # diag-fields-exempt: threaded constant
```

- field-presence pass: clean (opt-out honoured)
- spec_ref pass: `spec_ref is not a string literal — the gate cannot validate it`

The marker is present, carries a reason, and is ignored. The suggested fix ("make
it a literal") is also unfollowable when the value is a parameter or a module
constant.

## Why it is worth fixing

The gate exists to make "is every diagnostic fully tagged?" a mechanically
checkable contract. A gate whose own escape hatch does not work in two of three
passes is emitting advice that cannot be followed — the same "reports something
that isn't so" class the gate was built to catch.

Pre-existing; byte-identical on `main` before and after #827's narrowing (#952).
Surfaced by the adversarial review of #952 and verified against the current tree.

## Design question (why this is not a mechanical fix)

The opt-out currently means "this site is allowed to omit a required field". It is
not obvious it should also mean "this site is allowed to cite a spec section that
does not exist" or "this site is allowed to emit an unregistered error_code" —
those are content errors, not tagging omissions, and blanket-suppressing them
would weaken the gate.

Two coherent options:

1. **Honour the opt-out in all three passes.** Simple and consistent with the
   advertised contract; accepts that a reasoned opt-out can suppress a bogus
   `spec_ref` / unregistered `error_code`.
2. **Narrow the advice.** Keep the opt-out presence-only, and stop offering it in
   the report for `spec_ref` / `error_code` violations. For the specific
   "`spec_ref` is not a string literal" complaint, either drop the complaint (a
   threaded value genuinely cannot be validated statically, and the presence pass
   already accepts it) or emit a followable fix.

Option 2 preserves the gate's strength; option 1 preserves its advertised
contract. Worth deciding deliberately rather than by accident.

## Acceptance criteria

- The three passes and the failure report agree on what `# diag-fields-exempt`
  does.

problem_statement.title: [BUG] ViewerFile.is_running() returns True after viewer.close() -- because it's not implemented
problem_statement.body:
### Bug Description

When using `Newton.Viewer.ViewerGL`, calling `viewer.close()` changes some internal flag such that `viewer.is_running()` returns False afterwards, as would be suggested by the function names. However, this is not the case with `ViewerFile`: even after `viewer.close()` is called, `viewer.is_running()` continues to return True.

Looking at the code, this is because`ViewerFile` does not implement `is_running()`, and in `ViewerBase` the default behavior is to return True. Thus, it seems like an easy fix could be to just add a flag to `ViewerFile` to track whether `ViewerFile.close()` has been called.

This inconsistency/bug causes an issue when a main simulation loop is implemented as:
```
while viewer.is_running(): 
    ...
```
This while loop can be terminated by `viewer.close()` when `viewer` is an instance of `ViewerGL`, but this termination no longer works if `viewer` is an instance of `ViewerFile`. Being able to easily swap between viewer types while using this pattern seems like something that is worth supporting...?

I have attached a reproduction script for reproducing this issue. It is a modified version of `example_recording.py`. If you set `HEADLESS` on line 129 to True, then Newton will run with `ViewerFile`, and you will see that although the log file is saved when the max frame count is reached and thus `viewer.close()`is called, the simulation loop will continue, and frames will continue to be saved. If you set `HEADLESS` to False, then Newton will correctly terminate after the maximum frame count has been exceeded.

I can submit a PR for this soon, if this is a problem deemed worth fixing and a contribution is welcome. Just let me know!

### Reproduction Script
This is a modified version of `example_recording.py` made to show how the current lack of a `viewer.is_running()` implementation for `ViewerFile` prevents workflows that have easy switching between a GUI render mode and a headless log-file mode.

Changes were only made near the end of the file. There is a comment indicating where changes were made.

```python
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2025 The Newton Developers
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

###########################################################################
# Example Recording
#
# Shows how to record a simulation using ViewerFile for automatic recording
# of model structure and state data during simulation.
#
# Recording happens automatically - ViewerFile captures all logged states
# and saves them when the viewer is closed.
#
# Command: python -m newton.examples recording
#
###########################################################################

import numpy as np
import warp as wp

import newton
import newton.examples


class Example:
    def __init__(self, viewer, _args):
        # Setup simulation parameters
        self.fps = 60
        self.frame_dt = 1.0 / self.fps
        self.sim_time = 0.0
        self.sim_substeps = 10
        self.sim_dt = self.frame_dt / self.sim_substeps

        self.viewer = viewer
        self.world_count = 100

        # Set numpy random seed for reproducibility
        self.seed = 123
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(self.seed)

        start_rot = wp.quat_from_axis_angle(wp.normalize(wp.vec3(*self.rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0, size=3))), -wp.pi * 0.5)

        mjcf_filename = newton.examples.get_asset("nv_humanoid.xml")

        articulation_builder = newton.ModelBuilder()
        articulation_builder.add_mjcf(
            mjcf_filename,
            ignore_names=["floor", "ground"],
            up_axis="Z",
        )

        # Joint initial positions
        articulation_builder.joint_q[:7] = [0.0, 0.0, 1.5, *start_rot]

        builder = newton.ModelBuilder()
        for _i in range(self.world_count):
            articulation_builder.joint_q[7:] = self.rng.uniform(
                -1.0, 1.0, size=(len(articulation_builder.joint_q) - 7,)
            ).tolist()
            builder.add_world(articulation_builder)
        builder.add_ground_plane()

        # Finalize model
        self.model = builder.finalize()
        self.control = self.model.control()

        self.solver = newton.solvers.SolverMuJoCo(
            self.model,
            use_mujoco_cpu=False,
            solver="newton",
            integrator="euler",
            iterations=10,
            ls_iterations=5,
            njmax=100,
        )

        self.state_0, self.state_1 = self.model.state(), self.model.state()

        self.use_cuda_graph = wp.get_device().is_cuda

        if self.use_cuda_graph:
            with wp.ScopedCapture() as capture:
                self.simulate()
            self.graph = capture.graph

        # Set model in viewer (ViewerFile will automatically record it)
        self.viewer.set_model(self.model)

    def simulate(self):
        for _ in range(self.sim_substeps):
            self.state_0.clear_forces()
            self.solver.step(self.state_0, self.state_1, self.control, None, self.sim_dt)
            self.state_0, self.state_1 = self.state_1, self.state_0

    def step(self):
        with wp.ScopedTimer("step", active=False):
            if self.use_cuda_graph:
                wp.capture_launch(self.graph)
            else:
                self.simulate()
        self.sim_time += self.frame_dt

    def render(self):
        self.viewer.begin_frame(self.sim_time)
        self.viewer.log_state(self.state_0)  # ViewerFile automatically records this
        self.viewer.end_frame()

    def test_final(self):
        pass


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Create ViewerFile for automatic recording
    import sys

    recording_file = "humanoid_recording.bin"

    # Check if user wants a different filename from command line
    if len(sys.argv) > 1 and not sys.argv[1].startswith("-"):
        recording_file = sys.argv[1]

    print(f"Recording simulation to: {recording_file}")
    print("ViewerFile will automatically save when the simulation ends.")

    parser = newton.examples.create_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args()

    # -------------------------- BELOW IS THE CHANGED SECTION TO SHOW BUG --------------------------
    HEADLESS = True #CHANGE THIS TO TOGGLE BEHAVIOR
    if HEADLESS:
        viewer = newton.viewer.ViewerFile(recording_file, auto_save=False)
    else:
        viewer = newton.viewer.ViewerGL(headless=False)

    # Create example
    example = Example(viewer, args)

    # Run for a reasonable number of frames
    max_frames = 1000
    frame_count = 0

    # while frame_count < max_frames:
    while viewer.is_running():
        example.step()
        example.render()
        frame_count += 1

        if frame_count % 100 == 0:
            print(f"Frame {frame_count}/{max_frames}")
        
        if frame_count >= max_frames:
            viewer.close()


    # Close viewer (automatically saves recording)
    # viewer.close()
    print(f"Recording completed: {recording_file}")
```

### System Information

- Newton version: commit a046d613
- Python version: 3.11.14
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.3
- Kernel: 6.17.0-29 generic
- GPU: RTX4070 mobile
- Nvidia driver: 580.159.03
- CUDA version: 13.0

issue_title: release_check_m3.sh: hermes harness should soft-fail when model context < 64K (same pattern as smolagents)
gold_patch:
diff --git a/vllm_mlx/agents/testing.py b/vllm_mlx/agents/testing.py
index 875f9587d8..24aec047e9 100644
--- a/vllm_mlx/agents/testing.py
+++ b/vllm_mlx/agents/testing.py
@@ -740,6 +740,37 @@ def _agent_query(
         output = proc.stdout + proc.stderr
         if "error" in output.lower() and "HTTP 4" in output:
             return None, "Agent error: server issue"
+        # Harness self-refuses to initialize when the served model's
+        # advertised context window is below what the harness's tool-rich
+        # system prompt requires (issue #655 — Hermes hard-requires 64K;
+        # qwen3.5-4b/9b-4bit advertise 32K, so init always fails on those).
+        # The subprocess exits 0 and writes the refusal to stdout, so
+        # without this check downstream tests see "no expected substring"
+        # and report FAIL — which is dishonest, it's a harness-config
+        # mismatch, not a rapid-mlx regression. Propagate as SKIP via the
+        # ``SKIP:``-prefixed err sentinel that each ``_test_e2e_*`` already
+        # honors.
+        if "Failed to initialize agent" in output and "context window" in output:
+            # Extract the first matching line from the subprocess output so
+            # the resulting TestResult.message carries the actual model
+            # name + advertised vs minimum token counts (codex NIT #659).
+            # Without this, the user sees a generic "below the harness
+            # minimum" and has to dig in the server log to learn which
+            # model and what numbers — the very signal that makes this
+            # actionable.
+            refusal_line = next(
+                (
+                    line.strip()
+                    for line in output.splitlines()
+                    if "Failed to initialize agent" in line
+                ),
+                "",
+            )
+            detail = f": {refusal_line[:200]}" if refusal_line else ""
+            return None, (
+                f"SKIP: agent refused init — served model's context window "
+                f"is below the harness minimum{detail}"
+            )
         return output, None
     except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
         return None, "TIMEOUT"
@@ -747,6 +778,27 @@ def _agent_query(

diff --git a/tests/test_agent_query_context_skip.py b/tests/test_agent_query_context_skip.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..0f0ef981d7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_agent_query_context_skip.py
@@ -0,0 +1,226 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Pin the soft-skip behavior when a harness refuses init on context window.
+
+Regression coverage for issue #655: the v0.7.27 release SOP's M3 gauntlet
+G7b aborted because Hermes Agent refuses to initialize on Qwen3.5-9B-4bit
+(advertised context window 32K, Hermes minimum 64K). The subprocess
+exited 0 and wrote the refusal to stdout, so before this fix:
+
+  - ``_agent_query`` returned ``(output, None)``
+  - ``_test_e2e_file_read`` saw "no expected substring" and reported FAIL
+  - The harness sweep ended 27p 7f 0e 0s and ``set -e`` aborted the gauntlet
+
+After the fix, ``_agent_query`` detects the refusal pattern and propagates
+a ``SKIP:``-prefixed err sentinel; the three ``_test_e2e_*`` callers
+honor that prefix and report SKIP instead of FAIL. The harness sweep
+stays honest (0 FAIL, N SKIP) and the gauntlet continues to the
+remaining gates.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+from vllm_mlx.agents.testing import (
+    TestStatus,
+    _agent_query,
+    _err_to_status,
+    _test_e2e_chat,
+    _test_e2e_file_read,
+    _test_e2e_terminal,
+)
+
+
+def _stub_completed_proc(stdout: str = "", stderr: str = "", returncode: int = 0):
+    """Build a stand-in for the subprocess.run() result."""
+
+    class _Stub:
+        def __init__(self):
+            self.stdout = stdout
+            self.stderr = stderr
+            self.returncode = returncode
+
+    return _Stub()
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+# _err_to_status: the three-bucket mapping                                    #
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+
+
+def test_err_to_status_not_found_is_skip():
+    assert _err_to_status("Binary not found: hermes") is TestStatus.SKIP
+
+
+def test_err_to_status_skip_prefix_is_skip():
+    assert (
+        _err_to_status("SKIP: agent refused init — context window") is TestStatus.SKIP
+    )
+
+
+def test_err_to_status_timeout_is_error():
+    assert _err_to_status("TIMEOUT") is TestStatus.ERROR
+
+
+def test_err_to_status_arbitrary_is_error():
+    assert _err_to_status("Agent error: server issue") is TestStatus.ERROR
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+# _agent_query: the detection happens once at the subprocess boundary         #
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+
+
+HERMES_REFUSAL_STDOUT = (
+    "Failed to initialize agent: Model mlx-community/Qwen3.5-9B-4bit has a "
+    "context window of 32,768 tokens, which is below the minimum 64,000 "
+    "required by Hermes Agent.\n"
+)
+
+
+def test_agent_query_detects_context_refusal_as_skip():
+    """The Hermes-style "context window below minimum" refusal → SKIP err."""
+    with (
+        patch("vllm_mlx.agents.testing.shutil.which", return_value="/fake/hermes"),
+        patch(
+            "vllm_mlx.agents.testing.subprocess.run",
+            return_value=_stub_completed_proc(stdout=HERMES_REFUSAL_STDOUT),
+        ),
+    ):
+        out, err = _agent_query(
+            "hermes", "hermes chat -q '{query}' -Q", "hi", timeout=10
+        )
+    assert out is None, (
+        "On refusal, output must be suppressed so downstream tests route via err"
+    )
+    assert err is not None
+    assert err.startswith("SKIP:"), (
+        f"Refusal must be propagated with a SKIP: prefix so _test_e2e_* "
+        f"recognize it; got err={err!r}"
+    )
+    # The actionable bits — model name and the actual vs required token
+    # counts — must survive into the SKIP message (codex NIT #659).
+    # Without them, the user has to dig in the server log to learn what
+    # the harness wanted vs what the model offered.
+    assert "Qwen3.5-9B-4bit" in err, (
+        f"SKIP message must carry the model name; got err={err!r}"
+    )
+    assert "32,768" in err and "64,000" in err, (
+        f"SKIP message must carry the advertised vs minimum context values; "
+        f"got err={err!r}"
+    )
+
+
+def test_agent_query_passes_through_normal_output():
+    """A clean subprocess success returns ``(output, None)`` as before."""
+    with (
+        patch("vllm_mlx.agents.testing.shutil.which", return_value="/fake/codex"),
+        patch(
+            "vllm_mlx.agents.testing.subprocess.run",
+            return_value=_stub_completed_proc(stdout="The answer is 4.\n"),
+        ),
+    ):
+        out, err = _agent_query(
+            "codex", "codex -q '{query}'", "what is 2+2?", timeout=10
+        )
+    assert err is None
+    assert out is not None and "4" in out
+
+
+def test_agent_query_does_not_match_unrelated_failures():
+    """\"Failed to initialize agent\" alone (no \"context window\") is NOT a SKIP.
+
+    Other init failures (missing API key, bad config, etc) should remain
+    ERROR — auto-skipping would mask real harness regressions.
+    """
+    bad_init_no_context = (
+        "Failed to initialize agent: missing OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable\n"
+    )
+    with (
+        patch("vllm_mlx.agents.testing.shutil.which", return_value="/fake/hermes"),
+        patch(
+            "vllm_mlx.agents.testing.subprocess.run",
+            return_value=_stub_completed_proc(stdout=bad_init_no_context),
+        ),
+    ):
+        out, err = _agent_query(
+            "hermes", "hermes chat -q '{query}' -Q", "hi", timeout=10
+        )
+    # Output passes through (not None); downstream tests then route via
+    # "no expected substring" → FAIL, which is the correct signal for a
+    # genuine harness misconfiguration.
+    assert err is None
+    assert out is not None and "OPENAI_API_KEY" in out
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+# Each of the three _test_e2e_* functions must route SKIP-prefixed err → SKIP #
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
+
+
+def test_e2e_chat_routes_skip_prefix_to_skip_status():
+    with (
+        patch("vllm_mlx.agents.testing.shutil.which", return_value="/fake/hermes"),
+        patch(
+            "vllm_mlx.agents.testing.subprocess.run",
+            return_value=_stub_completed_proc(stdout=HERMES_REFUSAL_STDOUT),
+        ),
+    ):
+        result = _test_e2e_chat("hermes", "hermes chat -q '{query}' -Q", timeout=10)
+    assert result.status is TestStatus.SKIP, (
+        f"e2e_chat must SKIP on Hermes context-window refusal (#655), not FAIL/ERROR. "
+        f"Got status={result.status}, message={result.message!r}"
+    )
+
+
+def test_e2e_file_read_routes_skip_prefix_to_skip_status():
+    """Direct regression for the gauntlet line in #655."""
+    with (
+        patch("vllm_mlx.agents.testing.shutil.which", return_value="/fake/hermes"),
+        patch(
+            "vllm_mlx.agents.testing.subprocess.run",
+            return_value=_stub_completed_proc(stdout=HERMES_REFUSAL_STDOUT),
+        ),
+    ):
+        result = _test_e2e_file_read(
+            "hermes", "hermes chat -q '{query}' -Q", timeout=10
+        )
+    assert result.status is TestStatus.SKIP
+    assert "context window" in (result.message or "").lower() or "context window" in (
+        result.message or ""
+    )
+
+
+def test_e2e_terminal_routes_skip_prefix_to_skip_status():
+    with (
+        patch("vllm_mlx.agents.testing.shutil.which", return_value="/fake/hermes"),
+        patch(
+            "vllm_mlx.agents.testing.subprocess.run",
+            return_value=_stub_completed_proc(stdout=HERMES_REFUSAL_STDOUT),
+        ),
+    ):
+        result = _test_e2e_terminal(
+            "hermes", "hermes chat -q '{query}' -Q", timeout=10, agent_name="hermes"
+        )
+    assert result.status is TestStatus.SKIP
+
+
+def test_e2e_tests_still_error_on_genuine_failure():
+    """A real subprocess crash must still be ERROR, not SKIP — guards against
+    over-broad SKIP routing masking regressions."""
+    with (
+        patch("vllm_mlx.agents.testing.shutil.which", return_value="/fake/hermes"),
+        patch(
+            "vllm_mlx.agents.testing.subprocess.run",
+            side_effect=TimeoutError("simulated timeout"),
+        ),
+    ):
+        result = _test_e2e_file_read("hermes", "hermes chat -q '{query}' -Q", timeout=1)
+    # TimeoutError raised inside _agent_query → caught by the bare ``except
+    # Exception`` and turned into err=str(exc); the resulting err is NOT
+    # "not found" and does NOT start with "SKIP:", so the test routes to
+    # ERROR — which is the correct signal for a genuine subprocess failure.
+    assert result.status is TestStatus.ERROR, (
+        f"A genuine subprocess failure must remain ERROR (not SKIP). "

problem_statement.title: release_check_m3.sh: hermes harness should soft-fail when model context < 64K (same pattern as smolagents)
problem_statement.body:
## Symptom

On v0.7.27 release SOP run, M3 gauntlet bailed at G7b Part A (\`bench --tier harness\`) because the Hermes harness refused to initialize:

\`\`\`
FAIL hermes (34.1s) 27p 7f 0e 0s | e2e_file_read: Failed to initialize agent: Model mlx-community/Qwen3.5-9B-4bit has a context window of 32,768 tokens, which is below the minimum 64,000 required by Hermes Agent.
\`\`\`

Same on \`mlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-MLX-4bit\` (also 32K context).

\`set -e\` propagates the failure, so the gauntlet aborts before reaching G6 / G9 / G8, even though every gate that CAN pass on the model has passed (codex / opencode / aider / langchain all PASS, plus G1 / G5 / G7 Anthropic / pydantic_ai / smolagents informational, plus the standalone LangChain 6/6).

## Root cause

Hermes Agent (\`AgentTestRunner\`) has a hard 64K minimum context requirement. The MLX-community Qwen3.5 \"verified-tier\" set has 4B (32K) and 9B (32K) variants only; no variant in our default release-validation set hits 64K. Hermes init is **always** going to fail on these.

The release gauntlet script (\`scripts/release_check_m3.sh\`) explicitly soft-fails smolagents tests 3+4 with a documented \`|| true\` because they're known-422-by-design under \`tool_choice=required\`. It needs the same treatment for Hermes when the underlying model's context_window < 64K.

## Fix options

**A** — Make Hermes skip-not-fail when context_window < 64K (inside \`bench --tier harness\`). This is the right place: a context-eligibility check belongs to the harness layer, not the gauntlet wrapper. Same pattern as DFlash's \`check(profile, alias=name)\` raising \`DFlashUnavailable\` cleanly.

**B** — Add \`|| true\` on the \`bench --tier harness\` line in \`release_check_m3.sh\` ONLY for hermes (i.e. accept the FAIL but document it as expected). Easier but weaker — any future harness regression in codex/opencode/aider/langchain would also be auto-skipped.

Recommend **A**.

## Workaround for now

Set \`READY_TIMEOUT=240\` and run with a 64K+ context model (Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit has 64K). Or simply skip the harness tier check on small-context-model release gates.

## v0.7.27 status

Release was shipped (PyPI + Homebrew published). Every gate that CAN pass on Qwen3.5-9B-4bit DID pass. R2 mirror was end-to-end validated on 8+ alias pulls including a VLM. The gauntlet's silent termination at hermes is a gauntlet ergonomic gap, not a v0.7.27 code regression.

## Related

- \`scripts/release_check_m3.sh\` lines ~150-175 (G7b Part A invocation)
- The DFlash-style \`DFlashUnavailable\` precedent in \`vllm_mlx/cli.py:serve_command\` (clean error vs hard exit on init refusal)
- Smolagents soft-fail comment in \`release_check_m3.sh\` (~line 90)

problem_statement.title: View column tags not applied on the ALTER update path (view_update_via_alter: true) → "main is not being called" error
problem_statement.body:
### Describe the bug

A Unity Catalog view configured with `view_update_via_alter: true` and column-level `databricks_tags` fails on a subsequent `dbt run` whose only change is its column tags, with:

```
Runtime Error in model <model> (models/<model>.sql)
  main is not being called during running model
```

The create path applies column tags correctly; only the `ALTER` update path is affected.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `use_materialization_v2: true`, and the model configured with `+view_update_via_alter: true`.
2. A view model with column-level `databricks_tags` on a column.
3. `dbt run` — the view is created and the tags are applied. ✅
4. Change only the column tags (e.g. add a tag to another column), then `dbt run` again. ❌

### Expected behavior

The changed column tags are applied to the view on the `ALTER` update path, matching the create path and the `table` / V2 materialization paths.

### Actual behavior

`dbt run` errors with `main is not being called during running model`.

### Root cause

`databricks__alter_view` (`dbt/include/databricks/macros/relations/view/alter.sql`) handles `tags`, `tblproperties`, `query`, and `column_comments` from the configuration changeset but has no branch for `column_tags` — while `ViewConfig.config_components` includes `ColumnTagsProcessor` and a column-tags-only change does not set `requires_full_refresh` (so it routes to `alter_view` rather than a full replace). When column tags are the only change, the macro becomes a no-op that never calls `statement('main')`, which dbt treats as an error.

### Scope

Only affects views with `view_update_via_alter: true` (non-default) that use column tags. The create path and the `table` / V2-incremental paths are unaffected. The analogous V1-incremental column-tags drop is tracked in #1307 (fixed in #1520).

### System information

- **dbt-databricks**: main
- **Platform**: Unity Catalog

problem_statement.body:
To my understanding in create_reference_model()
https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/9b3c5bf64fd88526481ec32de85539e2bbdda92b/trl/models/modeling_base.py#L662-L668

when (frozen) layers are shared with the reference model they are still copied and held in memory twice. Memory can be saved by referencing the tensor data like:
`_ref_param.data = param.data`

From the code comment this is the intention of this loop but I don't see how `_ref_param = ref_model.get_parameter(param_name)` achieves this except some magic is happening elsewhere.

An old version of this loop featured `_ref_param = param` but this also does not lead to a permanent reference of the model parameter.

title: Fix YAML octal/hex corruption of unquoted DTMF sequences in eval scenarios

new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/changelog/4887.fixed.md
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+- Fixed eval scenarios silently corrupting unquoted DTMF turns with leading zeros or a hex prefix. YAML 1.1 parsed `dtmf: 012` as octal (`10`) and `dtmf: 0x10` as hex before validation, sending the wrong keypresses; the scenario loader now resolves only plain-decimal scalars as integers, so leading-zero sequences keep their digits and `dtmf: 123` still works.
diff --git a/src/pipecat/evals/scenario.py b/src/pipecat/evals/scenario.py
index d0502946ee2..ffe5c93b6e2 100644
--- a/src/pipecat/evals/scenario.py
+++ b/src/pipecat/evals/scenario.py
@@ -123,6 +123,7 @@
     judge: !include judge_audio.yaml
 """
 
+import re
 from dataclasses import dataclass, field
 from pathlib import Path
 from typing import Any
@@ -133,6 +134,37 @@
 
 from pipecat.audio.dtmf.types import KeypadEntry
 
+
+class _ScenarioLoader(yaml.SafeLoader):
+    """SafeLoader that resolves only plain-decimal numeric scalars as ints.
+
+    PyYAML's SafeLoader follows YAML 1.1, which reinterprets unquoted numeric
+    scalars as octal (``010`` -> 8), hex (``0x10`` -> 16), or binary before
+    application code sees them. For DTMF that silently rewrites the digit
+    sequence the user typed (``dtmf: 012`` would load as ``10``). Dropping those
+    resolvers and keeping only plain decimal means ``dtmf: 123`` still loads as
+    an int (so the unquoted-digits convenience works), while leading-zero, hex,
+    and binary tokens stay strings and reach DTMF validation with their digits
+    intact. No scenario field wants an octal/hex literal, so this is safe
+    document-wide.
+    """
+
+
+# Strip the inherited int resolvers (which match octal/hex/binary/sexagesimal)
+# and register a decimal-only replacement. Underscores stay allowed to match
+# YAML's grouping syntax (e.g. ``1_000``); a leading zero (``012``) no longer
+# matches, so such tokens load as strings.
+_ScenarioLoader.yaml_implicit_resolvers = {
+    ch: [(tag, rx) for tag, rx in resolvers if tag != "tag:yaml.org,2002:int"]
+    for ch, resolvers in yaml.SafeLoader.yaml_implicit_resolvers.items()
+}
+yaml.add_implicit_resolver(
+    "tag:yaml.org,2002:int",
+    re.compile(r"^[-+]?(?:0|[1-9][0-9_]*)$"),
+    list("-+0123456789"),
+    Loader=_ScenarioLoader,
+)
+
 # Events whose payloads carry bot-generated text the judge can sensibly
 # evaluate. Asserting ``eval:`` on anything else (user transcripts, tool
 # calls, interruption signals) produces a parser warning — the test controls
@@ -326,7 +358,7 @@ def load(cls, path: str | Path) -> "EvalScenario":
         # scenarios can share judge/user config. Includes resolve relative to the
         # scenario file's directory. Register the constructor on a private loader
         # subclass (not the global SafeLoader) so it has no global side effects.
-        class _Loader(yaml.SafeLoader):
+        class _Loader(_ScenarioLoader):
             pass
 
         YamlIncludeConstructor.add_to_loader_class(loader_class=_Loader, base_dir=str(path.parent))

+        YAML 1.1 would otherwise parse `012` as octal 10, silently sending the
+        wrong keys; the scenario loader resolves only plain decimal as int.
+        """
+        for seq in ("012", "010", "007", "0420", "000"):
+            s = EvalScenario.load(_write(f"name: dtmf\nturns: [{{dtmf: {seq}}}]\n"))
+            self.assertEqual(s.turns[0].dtmf, seq)
+
+    def test_dtmf_unquoted_hex_rejected(self):
+        """A hex-looking token isn't read as a number; `x` fails validation."""
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as cm:
+            EvalScenario.load(_write("name: bad\nturns: [{dtmf: 0x10}]\n"))
+        self.assertIn("invalid keypad entry", str(cm.exception))
+
     def test_dtmf_invalid_entry_rejected(self):
         with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as cm:
             EvalScenario.load(_write('name: bad\nturns: [{dtmf: "1A"}]\n'))

problem_statement.title: [Detail Bug] YAML DTMF values like 010 or 0x10 are silently changed into different key sequences
problem_statement.body:
# Detail Bug Report

https://app.detail.dev/org_1fa3c5ff-f485-452b-8fbd-870cbd985e00/bugs/bug_c1e2830c-ee35-4567-a146-b513c54a14e5

Introduced in [#4849](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/pull/4849) by @aconchillo on Jun 22, 2026

# Summary
- **Context**: The framework supports unquoted integer DTMF but corrupts YAML octal (`010` → `"8"`) and hex (`0x10` → `"16"`) values.
- **Bug**: The framework supports unquoted integer DTMF but corrupts YAML octal (`010` → `"8"`) and hex (`0x10` → `"16"`) values.
- **Actual vs. expected**: **Expected**: `dtmf: 010` is treated as the digit sequence `"010"` (three keypresses), and `dtmf: 0x10` is treated as `"0x10"`. **Actual**: YAML 1.1 SafeLoader parses these as integers (`8` and `16`), and the framework coerces them to strings (`"8"`, `"16"`), silently changing the DTMF sequence while still passing validation.
- **Impact**: Silent corruption of DTMF sequences (especially leading-zero PINs / sequences) causes scenarios/tests to send the wrong keys without any load-time error or warning, making failures confusing to debug.

# Code with Bug
```python
def _parse_dtmf(dtmf: Any, path: Path, turn_idx: int) -> str | None:
    if dtmf is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(dtmf, int):
        dtmf = str(dtmf)  # <-- BUG 🔴 silently normalizes YAML 1.1 octal/hex ints, losing original digit sequence
    # ... rest of validation
```

# Explanation
- PyYAML 6.0.3 `SafeLoader` implements YAML 1.1 numeric rules, which interpret values like `010` as octal and `0x10` as hex *before* application code sees them.
- By the time `_parse_dtmf` runs, it receives `int(8)` / `int(16)` and cannot recover the original token (`"010"` / `"0x10"`). Coercing to string therefore produces the wrong DTMF sequence.
- This is silent because the resulting characters (e.g., `8`, `1`, `6`) are valid DTMF keys, so downstream validation does not fail.

## Codebase Inconsistency
- The framework both (a) tests support for unquoted integer DTMF (e.g., `dtmf: 123`) and (b) documents quoting DTMF values, yet currently provides no warning/error for the YAML 1.1 octal/hex cases that silently change meaning.

# Recommended Fix
Add a warning when `dtmf` arrives as an `int` to alert users that YAML 1.1 may have rewritten their input (octal/hex) and to quote DTMF strings to preserve the intended sequence. A lower-noise variant is to warn only for small integers (`0..9`), which are the common outcomes of octal-like literals such as `010 → 8`.

# History
This bug was introduced in commit 02a01a82. The commit added DTMF turn support with integer-to-string coercion for convenience (`dtmf: 123` → `"123"`), but didn't account for YAML 1.1's octal (`010` → 8) and hex (`0x10` → 16) interpretation that silently corrupts leading-zero or hex-prefixed sequences.

problem_statement.title: [feature] define exe_wrapper for meson cross files
problem_statement.body:
### What is your suggestion?

Meson permits an `exe_wrapper` path in the `[binaries]` section of cross files.  This is used to run host binaries when cross-compiling. It is particularly important for unit tests; quoting from [the docs](https://mesonbuild.com/Cross-compilation.html#defining-the-environment):

"Meson must have exe_wrapper specified in the cross file or else **it will skip tests that attempt to run cross compiled binaries**." [emphasis mine]

Currently the `MesonToolchain` class does not provide a way to define this field.
It would be useful to define the wrapper path in my conan profile, and have it pass through to the generated meson cross file. For example:

```ini
# conan profile for host machine
# ...

[buildenv]
MESON_EXE_WRAPPER=/usr/bin/qemu-aarch64 -L /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu
# ...
```

```ini
# generated meson crossfile
# ...

[binaries]
exe_wrapper = ['/usr/bin/qemu-aarch64', '-L', '/usr/aarch64-linux-gnu']
# ...
```

Notes:
- `MesonToolchain` already sets the `needs_exe_wrapper` flag in the generated meson cross file, even though it doesn't provide a wrapper path
- "MESON_EXE_WRAPPER" is an appropriate env variable name for this purpose, as it is already used by meson to pass the path on down to test scripts.


I am willing to prepare a PR for this feature, but I may need some help writing tests for it. 

### Have you read the CONTRIBUTING guide?

- [x] I've read the CONTRIBUTING guide

problem_statement.title: hallways.py: _HALLWAY_FILE is hardcoded to ~/.mempalace/hallways.json, not palace-scoped
problem_statement.body:
`mempalace/hallways.py:52` hardcodes the hallway store path:

```python
_HALLWAY_FILE = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".mempalace", "hallways.json")
```

This path is not derived from `MempalaceConfig.palace_path`, so two palaces on one host share one global `hallways.json`. Mining hallways into one palace silently pollutes the others. `tunnels.json` was migrated to palace-scoped in 3.3.6; hallways didn't get the same treatment.

## Reproduction (mempalace 3.4.0)

```python
import os
os.environ["MEMPALACE_PALACE_PATH"] = "/tmp/a/palace"
from mempalace.config import MempalaceConfig
from mempalace import hallways
cfg = MempalaceConfig()
print(cfg.tunnel_file)        # /tmp/a/tunnels.json
print(hallways._HALLWAY_FILE) # ~/.mempalace/hallways.json

hallways._save_hallways([{"id": "hall_a", "wing": "wing_a", ...}])

os.environ["MEMPALACE_PALACE_PATH"] = "/tmp/b/palace"
cfg = MempalaceConfig()
print(cfg.tunnel_file)        # /tmp/b/tunnels.json    ← scoped
print(hallways._HALLWAY_FILE) # ~/.mempalace/hallways.json  ← unchanged

hallways._load_hallways()     # returns palace-a's records
```

## Suggested fix

Apply the `palace_graph._get_tunnel_file()` pattern: add `MempalaceConfig.hallway_file` resolving to `<dirname(palace_path)>/hallways.json`, read via `_get_hallway_file(config)`, with a `_legacy_hallway_file()` fallback that logs a one-line warning when the legacy file exists but the configured one doesn't. Keep atomic-write and 0600-perm semantics.

## Environment

- Verified against HEAD (`2ec4bae`) and v3.4.0 (`pip install mempalace==3.4.0`).
- Linux, Python 3.9.

## Related

- Discussion #1220 — multi-palace isolation. Names the same pattern for `known_entities.json` and `config.json`.
- #1454 — multi-palace deployment recipe docs (#832, #1096, #1043, #678, #1300).
- 3.3.6 tunnel-file scoping (`palace_graph._get_tunnel_file` + `_legacy_tunnel_file`) is the precedent worth matching.
- #1741 — exposed `list_hallways`/`delete_hallway` via MCP. Newly visible at the MCP surface.

+    """A per-line ``isort: skip`` must be honored even when a ``__future__`` import is present.
+

+    the sorted import block ahead of a following ``# isort: skip`` line and relocate the skipped

+    # An interleaved skip (between two regular imports) must keep its position rather than
+    # being sorted to the bottom of the block, and must be idempotent.
+    interleaved = "import aaa\nfrom foo import bar  # isort: skip\nimport ccc\n"
+    sorted_interleaved = isort.code(interleaved)
+    lines = sorted_interleaved.splitlines()
+    skip_index = next(i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if "# isort: skip" in line)
+    assert lines.index("import ccc") > skip_index  # skip not relocated below the block
+    assert isort.code(sorted_interleaved) == sorted_interleaved

problem_statement.title: `isort: skip` not working when futures imports are present
problem_statement.body:
## Bug summary
`isort: skip` seems to not work when there is a futures imports are present.


## Reproducible example

Running `isort test.py` on this example works well. No changes are made.

```python
# test.py
from foo import bar  # isort: skip
from bar import baz

baz + bar
```

When modifying the file to include a futures import:

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from foo import bar  # isort: skip
from bar import baz

baz + bar
```

isort now moves the marked import to the bottom.

problem_statement.title: Remove 0000 trace fallback
problem_statement.body:
In metrics and logs, we currently have a fallback for when there is no trace ID in the current trace context. We [set](<https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-python/blob/master/sentry_sdk/scope.py#L1864>) the trace_id since it's a required field to a dummy value.

This needs to be removed as it's causing issues (the nil trace ID telemetry is getting clustered into a huge trace) and there should never be a case where there is no trace ID.

We believe we shouldn't be hitting the fallback anymore in newer SDK versions due to the recent propagation context handling refactor but we need to verify if that's the case and then remove the fallback.

- [ ] find out when we hit the fallback and fix the code path so that it doesn't happen anymore
- [ ] remove the fallback

problem_statement.title: [BUG] VBD Cables Kinetic Energy Injection at Small Radius
problem_statement.body:
### Bug Description

Running the SolverVBD for cables at larger radius seems stable, but once the radius is small enough (e.g. 5mm for a 50cm long cable), the cable starts accumulating energy from somewhere after 4-5s. This did not happen in newton 1.2.1. See the attached simulation result, where the cable is simply dropped from an arbitrary height, and if the cable is not rotated, it stays in place (no accumulation of kinetic energy, printed in the reproduction script as output), but if the starting pose of the cable is slightly rotated in xy-plane, it will start moving due to some error accumulating.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea72cb66-fa0b-4f0c-8946-2d6a81300643

### Reproduction Script

```python
"""Minimal pure-Newton repro: two cables falling flat onto the ground.

Two straight cables (chains of capsule segments joined by cable joints, built with
``builder.add_rod``) are dropped horizontally onto a level floor, side by side:
one yawed 0 deg about world Z, one yawed 10 deg. They are offset in Y so they do
not touch.

Physical expectation: each should land and lie still, like a dropped rope. With the
rigid-contact-anchor bug, each capsule segment is an unstable contact (see
cylinder_two.py): a tiny perturbation is amplified instead of damped, so the
segments spuriously start rolling, the cable writhes/curls, and total kinetic
energy GROWS instead of decaying to rest.

Run (opens a GL window):
  PYTHONPATH=/home/mmichelis/Documents/newton-gilles \
    /home/mmichelis/Documents/IsaacLab-Origin/isaaclab.sh -p /tmp/cable_fall.py --viewer gl

Headless smoke test (prints the numbers):
  PYTHONPATH=/home/mmichelis/Documents/newton-gilles \
    /home/mmichelis/Documents/IsaacLab-Origin/isaaclab.sh -p /tmp/cable_fall.py --viewer null --num-frames 250
"""

import numpy as np
import warp as wp

import newton
import newton.examples

NUM_SEGMENTS = 20
SEGMENT_LENGTH = 0.5 / (NUM_SEGMENTS - 1)
RADIUS = 0.005
STRETCH_STIFFNESS = 1.0e6
STRETCH_DAMPING = 1.0e-4
BEND_STIFFNESS = 1.0e-4
BEND_DAMPING = 1.0e-4
DROP_GAP = 0.8
# (yaw about world Z [deg], Y-offset [m]) for each cable.
CABLES = [(0.0, -0.3), (10.0, 0.3)]


class Example:
    def __init__(self, viewer, args=None):
        self.viewer = viewer
        self.args = args

        self.fps = 100
        self.frame_dt = 1.0 / self.fps
        self.sim_time = 0.0
        self.sim_substeps = 8
        self.sim_dt = self.frame_dt / self.sim_substeps
        self.frame = 0

        builder = newton.ModelBuilder(gravity=-9.81, up_axis=newton.Axis.Z)

        cfg = newton.ModelBuilder.ShapeConfig()
        cfg.density = 100.0
        cfg.mu = 1.0
        cfg.ke = 1.0e3
        cfg.kd = 1.0e0
        cfg.kf = 0.0

        builder.add_shape_plane(body=-1, cfg=cfg)

        # Two horizontal cables, each yawed about world Z and offset in Y, dropped from DROP_GAP.
        length = NUM_SEGMENTS * SEGMENT_LENGTH
        start_z = RADIUS + DROP_GAP
        self.cables = []  # list of (label, body indices)
        for yaw_deg, y_off in CABLES:
            yaw = np.radians(yaw_deg)
            direction = wp.vec3(float(np.cos(yaw)), float(np.sin(yaw)), 0.0)
            center = wp.vec3(0.0, float(y_off), start_z)
            start0 = center - 0.5 * length * direction
            pts = newton.utils.create_straight_cable_points(
                start=start0, direction=direction, length=length, num_segments=NUM_SEGMENTS
            )
            edge_q = newton.utils.create_parallel_transport_cable_quaternions(pts, twist_total=0.0)
            bodies, _ = builder.add_rod(
                positions=pts,
                quaternions=edge_q,
                radius=RADIUS,
                cfg=cfg,
                stretch_stiffness=STRETCH_STIFFNESS,
                stretch_damping=STRETCH_DAMPING,
                bend_stiffness=BEND_STIFFNESS,
                bend_damping=BEND_DAMPING,
                label=f"cable_{yaw_deg:g}deg",
            )
            self.cables.append((f"{yaw_deg:g}deg", bodies))

        builder.color()
        self.model = builder.finalize()

        self.solver = newton.solvers.SolverVBD(
            self.model,
            iterations=20,
            rigid_contact_k_start=1.0e1,
            rigid_avbd_beta=1.0e2,
        )

        self.state_0 = self.model.state()
        self.state_1 = self.model.state()
        self.control = self.model.control()
        self.contacts = self.model.contacts()

        self.viewer.set_model(self.model)
        self.graph = None
        self.masses = self.model.body_mass.numpy()
        self.inertias = self.model.body_inertia.numpy()
        names = ", ".join(n for n, _ in self.cables)
        print(f"two cables ({names}); {NUM_SEGMENTS} segments each, length {length:.2f} m, radius {RADIUS} m")

    def _stats(self, q, qd, bodies):
        idx = np.array(bodies)
        mean_h = float(np.mean(q[idx, 2]))
        max_v = float(np.max(np.linalg.norm(qd[idx, 3:6], axis=1)))
        ke = 0.0
        for b in bodies:
            w, v = qd[b, 0:3], qd[b, 3:6]
            ke += 0.5 * float(self.masses[b]) * float(v @ v) + 0.5 * float(w @ (self.inertias[b] @ w))
        return mean_h, max_v, ke

    def simulate(self):
        for _ in range(self.sim_substeps):
            self.state_0.clear_forces()
            self.viewer.apply_forces(self.state_0)
            self.model.collide(self.state_0, self.contacts)
            self.solver.step(self.state_0, self.state_1, self.control, self.contacts, self.sim_dt)
            self.state_0, self.state_1 = self.state_1, self.state_0

    def step(self):
        self.simulate()
        self.sim_time += self.frame_dt
        if self.frame % 10 == 0:
            q = self.state_0.body_q.numpy()
            qd = self.state_0.body_qd.numpy()
            parts = []
            for name, bodies in self.cables:
                h, mv, ke = self._stats(q, qd, bodies)
                parts.append(f"{name}: h={h:.4f} |v|={mv:7.3f} KE={ke:.3e}")
            print(f"{self.frame:5d} | " + "  |  ".join(parts))
        self.frame += 1

    def render(self):
        self.viewer.begin_frame(self.sim_time)
        self.viewer.log_state(self.state_0)
        self.viewer.log_contacts(self.contacts, self.state_0)
        self.viewer.end_frame()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    viewer, args = newton.examples.init()
    newton.examples.run(Example(viewer, args), args)
```

### System Information

- newton: 1.3.0rc2
- warp: 1.14.0 (CUDA Toolkit 12.9)
- Python: 3.12.13
- OS: Linux 6.17.0-22 (x86_64, glibc 2.39)
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX A6000, driver 590.48.01

problem_statement.title: Binary StartsWith visitors compare bytes as strings
problem_statement.body:
Several `StartsWith` / `NotStartsWith` visitors appear to compare binary values by converting them with `str(...)`, which gives incorrect byte-prefix behavior.

Examples:

```text
StartsWith("x", b"a") on b"aa" -> False  # expected True
NotStartsWith("x", b"a") on b"aa" -> True # expected False
```

This also affects planning paths:

```text
inclusive metrics for a file containing only b"aa":
StartsWith("x", b"a") -> False  # unsafe skip
```

Manifest evaluation for binary `StartsWith` can also raise `TypeError` when comparing decoded `bytes` bounds to a `str` prefix.

Relevant code: `pyiceberg/expressions/visitors.py` starts-with handling in expression, manifest, metrics, and residual visitors.

+    """A caller-supplied `requests.Session` must be used for the provider-list

+    https://github.com/Materials-Consortia/optimade-python-tools/issues/2275

problem_statement.title: Client does not use configured HTTP session for scraping provider list
problem_statement.body:
The `get_all_databases` function does its own request handling. In cases where custom HTTP configurations are required (e.g., proxies etc.) this makes it impossible to use the client without manually setting the base URLs.

The `get_all_databases` (and related functions) could be refactored to use a custom HTTP client/session, but should default to doing their own thing (this function is called at initialisation of the reference server).

See #2274 for more info.

problem_statement.title: opentelemetry-sdk: NaN measurements permanently poison metric aggregations
problem_statement.body: ## Describe your environment ``` OS: Windows 11 Python version: 3.12.7 SDK version: 1.42.1 API version: 1.42.1 ``` ## What happened? When a `NaN` value is recorded on a metric instrument (e.g. `counter.add(float("nan"))`), it is silently folded into the running sum and permanently poisons that aggregation. Every subsequent export emits `nan` for that instrument, even if all future measurements are valid. The root cause: `SumAggregation` guards against negative values with `if amount < 0`, but `float("nan") < 0` evaluates to `False` in Python (all IEEE 754 comparisons against `NaN` return `False`), so `NaN` bypasses the guard and corrupts the running total. ## Steps to Reproduce ```python import math from opentelemetry import metrics from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics import MeterProvider from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export import InMemoryMetricReader reader = InMemoryMetricReader() provider = MeterProvider(metric_readers=[reader]) meter = provider.get_meter("test") counter = meter.create_counter("test_counter") counter.add(1) counter.add(float("nan")) # poisons the aggregation counter.add(5) # valid but sum is now nan metrics_data = reader.get_metrics_data() point = ( metrics_data.resource_metrics[0] .scope_metrics[0] .metrics[0] .data.data_points[0] ) print(f"sum = {point.value}") # sum = nan print(f"is nan = {math.isnan(point.value)}") # is nan = True ``` ## Expected Result The `NaN` measurement is dropped before aggregation. The counter continues accumulating valid measurements only. Final sum = `6.0`. ## Actual Result ``` sum = nan is nan = True ``` The aggregation is permanently corrupted , all subsequent exports for this instrument emit `nan` with no recovery path. ## Additional context The Java SDK hit the exact same issue in [open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java#5846](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java/issues/5846) and resolved it in [PR #5859](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java/pull/5859) (merged Sep 2023) by explicitly dropping `NaN` measurements at the SDK level before any aggregation occurs. The proposed fix for Python would be a `math.isnan` / `not math.isfinite` guard early in the `aggregate()` methods. one check per aggregation type, prevents permanent state corruption. Happy to implement this if the direction looks good. ## Would you like to implement a fix? Yes

+``smart_open.open('s3://bucket/key?versionId=v1')`` now extracts the ``versionId`` query parameter and forwards it as ``version_id`` to ``smart_open.s3.open``, matching the convention used by `s3fs <https://s3fs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#s3fs.core.S3FileSystem.split_path>`_ and the AWS CLI:
+
+.. code-block:: diff
+
+   - smart_open.open('s3://bucket/key', transport_params={'version_id': 'v1'})
+   + smart_open.open('s3://bucket/key?versionId=v1')
+
+Other ``?...`` content in the key is preserved as before (the ``QUESTION_MARK_PLACEHOLDER`` workaround in ``smart_open.utils.safe_urlsplit`` still keeps unrelated query strings attached to the key).
+``transport_params['version_id']`` still wins if both are set, with a ``UserWarning``.
+
+If you have a legitimate ``?versionId=...`` substring in your S3 key, call ``smart_open.s3.open(bucket, key, ...)`` directly with the raw key to bypass URI parsing.
+

problem_statement.title: [s3] Feature request: handle s3 url object versionId specifier
problem_statement.body:
#### Feature description

- What are you trying to achieve?

interoperability w/ url-like file specifiers that have the object version encoded in the path as `?versionId=...`

- What is the expected result?

this would return the correct version: `smart_open('s3://buckety/pathy-like-path.txt?versionId=12345')`

s3fs does this nicely: https://s3fs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#s3fs.core.S3FileSystem.split_path

- What are you seeing instead?

`smart_open` doesn't know that `?` can not be in an s3 key (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-keys.html), or that versionId is a valid url-parameter, so instead this type of open fails.


#### Checklist

Before you create the issue, please make sure you have:

- [x] Described the problem clearly
- [ ] Provided a minimal reproducible example, including any required data
- [ ] Provided the version numbers of the relevant software

problem_statement.title: tsql: EXECUTE @return_status = proc @args fails to parse (regression since v29.0.0)
problem_statement.body:
**Before you file an issue**
- [x] `read` dialect specified: `parse_one(sql, read="tsql")`
- [x] N/A — this is a parse-only issue, no `write`/`ast.sql(...)` involved
- [x] Confirmed still broken on latest release (30.12.0) and traced the regression back to v29.0.0 (see below)

**Fully reproducible code snippet**

```python
import sqlglot

sqlglot.parse("EXEC @RC = dbo.MyProc @a, @b;", read="tsql")

Raises:

sqlglot.errors.ParseError: Required keyword: 'this' missing for <class 'sqlglot.expressions.core.EQ'>. Line 1, Col: 23.
EXEC @RC = dbo.MyProc @a, @b;

The plain form without the return-status assignment parses fine:

sqlglot.parse("EXEC dbo.MyProc @a, @b;", read="tsql")  # OK

Also fails with no arguments at all, and with the unabbreviated keyword:

sqlglot.parse("EXEC @RC = dbo.MyProc;", read="tsql")            # ParseError
sqlglot.parse("EXECUTE @RC = dbo.MyProc @a, @b;", read="tsql")  # ParseError

**Official Documentation**

[EXECUTE (Transact-SQL)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/language-elements/execute-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17) — EXEC/EXECUTE supports an optional @return_status =  prefix that captures the stored procedure's return code:

[ [ EXEC [ UTE ] ]
    {
      [ @return_status = ]
      { module_name [ ;number ] | @module_name_var }
      ...

This is standard, widely used syntax, and sqlglot's tsql dialect fails to parse it.

+    """Attrs commands must not leak the ``attrs.NOTHING`` sentinel into help text.

+    """

+    """``takes_self`` factories cannot be resolved during introspection.

+    default: help must not show one (and must not leak the ``attrs.NOTHING``
+    sentinel), yet the factory still runs at construction time when no token is

+    https://github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/issues/857

problem_statement.title: Importing pydantic breaks Dataclass Commands
problem_statement.body:
This works if I invoke the command `test`:

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
#import pydantic

from cyclopts import App

app = App(result_action=["call_if_callable", "print_non_int_sys_exit"])

@app.command
@dataclass
class Test:
    numbers: list[int] = field(default_factory=lambda: [1,2,3])

    def __call__(self) -> str:
        return str(self.numbers)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()
```

```shell
python -m test test
[1, 2, 3]
```

If, however, I uncomment the line `import pydantic`, I get:
```shell
python -m test test
╭─ Error ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ 1 validation error for list[int]                                   │
│   Input should be a valid list [type=list_type,                    │
│ input_value=<factory>, input_type=_HAS_DEFAULT_FACTORY_CLASS]      │
│     For further information visit                                  │
│ https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.13/v/list_type                       │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

problem_statement.title: Add option to modify specific answer when `update`ing
problem_statement.body:
### Actual Situation

One of our template questions is a listing of all the internal dependencies of a project (they are excluded from min-age verifications and the like)

```yml
internal_dependencies:
  help: "Dependencies local to the org included in the project"
  default: []
```

when adding/removing an internal dependency to a project, a user has two options:
* Either they call `copier update`, and press `enter` a dozen times to update this one answer inline (the prompt is already filled in, so adding new entries to the list is easy).
* Or they call `copier update -A --data internal_dependencies=[...]` where `...` is the shorthand yaml syntax for the list (not as it appears in `.copier-answers.yml`), with the user's modification

Both are rather unwieldy

### Desired Situation

It would be easiest for to be able to skip all questions when `update`ing except for the few that the user knows ahead of time that they know they want to change.

### Proposed solution

introduce a new switch to `copier copy` named `--answer`, that the user may use to specify which questions they want to answer. acceptable values:
* `--answer=foo` answer only the question named `foo`
* `--answer=foo-*` answer only questions starting with `foo-*` (this is useful if the user wants to modify only some sub-section of the template)
* `--answer=a,b`, filters can be combined with a comma, in this case, only the questions `a` and `b` will b answered

In addition, `--answer` can include categories starting with a dollar sign, for example
* `--answer=$SHOWN` answer all non-hidden questions in the template (this can be considered the default value)
* `--answer=$UNANSWERED` answer only questions that haven't been previously answered (`-A` can be an alias for this)
* `--answer=` answer no questions (`--defaults` can be an alias for this)

When this argument is supplied to `copier copy`, it skips all questions that don't match any of the filters provided. Users can then call `copier update --answer=internal_dependencies` and they will only be prompted with the filled-in current value of `internal_dependencies`

title: fix(msword): don't abort conversion on a malformed hyperlink address
issue_title: msword/docx: malformed hyperlink address aborts the whole conversion

diff --git a/docling/backend/msword_backend.py b/docling/backend/msword_backend.py

@@ -36,7 +36,7 @@

-from pydantic import AnyUrl
+from pydantic import AnyUrl, ValidationError
 from typing_extensions import override

@@ -912,12 +912,34 @@ def _get_format_from_run(
         )
 
     def _get_hyperlink_target(self, hyperlink: Hyperlink) -> AnyUrl | Path | None:
+        """Resolve a hyperlink's address to a URL or a local path.
+
+        Addresses without a URL scheme are treated as (relative) filesystem
+        paths. Addresses with a scheme are parsed as URLs.
+
+        Malformed URLs (e.g. an address containing spaces) are handled
+        gracefully: the invalid target is dropped and ``None`` is returned so
+        that the link text is still preserved and conversion of the rest of the
+        document continues. This avoids a single bad hyperlink aborting the
+        whole conversion.
+
+        Args:
+            hyperlink: The DOCX hyperlink whose address should be resolved.
+
+        Returns:
+            An ``AnyUrl`` for a valid URL, a ``Path`` for a scheme-less address,
+            or ``None`` when there is no address or the URL is malformed.
+        """

-            return (
-                AnyUrl(hyperlink.address)
-                if urlparse(hyperlink.address).scheme
-                else Path(hyperlink.address)
-            )
+            if not urlparse(hyperlink.address).scheme:
+                return Path(hyperlink.address)
+            try:
+                return AnyUrl(hyperlink.address)
+            except ValidationError:
+                _log.warning(
+                    "Skipping malformed hyperlink address: %r", hyperlink.address
+                )
+                return None

+def test_malformed_hyperlink_does_not_abort_conversion(tmp_path):
+    """A single malformed hyperlink address (e.g. containing a space) must not
+    raise a pydantic ValidationError that aborts the whole DOCX conversion.
+
+    Regression test: previously ``_get_hyperlink_target`` called
+    ``AnyUrl(address)`` unguarded, so any address with a scheme but invalid
+    contents crashed the pipeline.
+    """
+    from docx import Document
+    from docx.opc.constants import RELATIONSHIP_TYPE as RT
+    from docx.oxml.ns import qn
+
+    doc = Document()
+    para = doc.add_paragraph("Before link. ")
+    # Ordinary real-world URL that happens to contain a space -> AnyUrl rejects it.
+    r_id = doc.part.relate_to(
+        "http://exa mple.com/bad url", RT.HYPERLINK, is_external=True
+    )
+    hyperlink = etree.SubElement(para._p, qn("w:hyperlink"))
+    hyperlink.set(qn("r:id"), r_id)
+    run = etree.SubElement(hyperlink, qn("w:r"))
+    etree.SubElement(run, qn("w:t")).text = "click me"
+    doc.add_paragraph("After link.")
+
+    docx_path = tmp_path / "malformed_hyperlink.docx"
+    doc.save(docx_path)
+
+    in_doc = InputDocument(
+        path_or_stream=docx_path,
+        format=InputFormat.DOCX,
+        backend=MsWordDocumentBackend,
+    )
+    result = in_doc._backend.convert()
+
+    # Conversion succeeds and the link's visible text is preserved.
+    md = result.export_to_markdown()
+    assert "click me" in md
+    assert "Before link." in md
+    assert "After link." in md
+
+    # The broken link target is dropped rather than crashing the run.
+    hyperlinks = [
+        item.hyperlink
+        for item, _ in result.iterate_items()
+        if isinstance(item, TextItem) and item.hyperlink is not None
+    ]
+    assert hyperlinks == []

### Bug
<!-- Describe the buggy behavior you have observed. -->

A single malformed hyperlink aborts the **entire** DOCX conversion.

If a document contains a hyperlink whose address is slightly malformed, most commonly a URL with a space in it, which happens constantly in real-world documents, the whole conversion shatters. One bad link takes down the entire document, not just that link, and no `DoclingDocument` is ever returned.

The conversion dies with:

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error
  Input should be a valid URL, invalid international domain name
  [type=url_parsing, input_value='http://exa mple.com/bad url', input_type=str]
```

Under the normal pipeline this surfaces as `RuntimeError: Pipeline SimplePipeline failed`.

**Expected result** one malformed hyperlink should degrade gracefully: keep the link's visible text and drop/leave-unresolved the broken target, and finish converting the rest of the document. Expected output for the repro below:

```
Before link. click me

After link.
```

### Steps to reproduce
<!-- Describe the sequence of steps for reproducing the bug. -->

Self-contained repro. It builds a `.docx` with one hyperlink whose address contains a space, then converts it. No external file needed:

```python
from pathlib import Path

from docx import Document
from docx.opc.constants import RELATIONSHIP_TYPE as RT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from lxml import etree

from docling.backend.msword_backend import MsWordDocumentBackend
from docling.datamodel.base_models import InputFormat
from docling.datamodel.document import InputDocument

OUT = Path("bad_hyperlink.docx")

doc = Document()
p = doc.add_paragraph("Before link. ")
# A perfectly ordinary real-world URL that happens to contain a space:
r_id = doc.part.relate_to("http://exa mple.com/bad url", RT.HYPERLINK, is_external=True)
hyperlink = etree.SubElement(p._p, qn("w:hyperlink"))
hyperlink.set(qn("r:id"), r_id)
run = etree.SubElement(hyperlink, qn("w:r"))
etree.SubElement(run, qn("w:t")).text = "click me"
doc.add_paragraph("After link.")
doc.save(OUT)

in_doc = InputDocument(
    path_or_stream=OUT, format=InputFormat.DOCX, backend=MsWordDocumentBackend
)
result = in_doc._backend.convert()  # <-- crashes here on `main`
print(result.export_to_markdown())
```

### Docling version
<!-- Copy the output of `docling --version`. -->

```
Docling version: 2.107.0
Docling Core version: 2.85.0
Docling Parse version: 7.0.0
Python: cpython-313 (3.13.6)
```

### Python version
<!-- Copy the output of `python --version`. -->

```
Python 3.13.6
```

problem_statement.title: [bug] CMakeConfigDeps renders self.cpp.build.component[...].location relative to package folder rather than build_folder
problem_statement.body:
### Describe the bug

When consuming a recipe that is configured as an editable package, CMakeConfigDeps renders the `self.cpp.build.component[...].location` field relative to the package folder rather than the build folder.

```
# This is the result ATM:
set_target_properties(App::test PROPERTIES IMPORTED_LOCATION_RELEASE "${app_PACKAGE_FOLDER_RELEASE}/Release/test.exe")

# This is what it I suspect it should be
set_target_properties(App::test PROPERTIES IMPORTED_LOCATION_RELEASE "${app_PACKAGE_FOLDER_RELEASE}/build/Release/test.exe")
```

Also - it's not clear from the documentation what the `cpp_info.exe` field is meant to reference.  There's 2 usages of it in the conan center, and it would appear that it should *just* refer to the name of the executable (without path and extension??).

Similarly, the `cpp_info.location` documentation suggests that it should refer to the "full location (path and filename with extension) of the artifact".  The conan center usages actually explicitly prefix the location path with `self.package_folder` to make it an absolute (i.e. "full") path, but I suspect they should probably not be doing that.  It might suggest that the documentation could be refined to better describe the field (or I could be wrong with *my* assumption!)

I'm running Conan 2.29.0 on Windows.

### How to reproduce it

_No response_

-def extract_parameter_filters(workspace_obj: FabricWorkspace, param_dict: dict) -> tuple[str, str, Path]:
+def extract_parameter_filters(
+    workspace_obj: FabricWorkspace, param_dict: dict
+) -> tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str], Optional[list[Path]]]:
     """Extracts the item type, name, and path filters from the parameter dictionary, if present."""
     item_type = param_dict.get("item_type")
     item_name = param_dict.get("item_name")
-    file_path = process_input_path(workspace_obj.repository_directory, param_dict.get("file_path"))
+    file_path = _resolve_filter_path(workspace_obj, param_dict.get("file_path"))
 
     return item_type, item_name, file_path
 
 
+def _resolve_filter_path(
+    workspace_obj: FabricWorkspace, file_path_filter: Union[str, list[str], None]
+) -> Union[list[Path], None]:
+    """
+    Resolves a parameter ``file_path`` filter to concrete repository paths, memoizing the result.
+
+    The resolved path set depends only on ``(repository_directory, file_path filter)``, both of which
+    are invariant across every file processed in a single publish. Without memoization, a wildcard
+    filter re-globs the entire repository once per file per parameter entry, producing super-linear
+    (effectively quadratic) filesystem traversal on large repositories. Caching the result keyed on the
+    filter makes the repository glob run once per unique filter instead.
+    """
+    cache = getattr(workspace_obj, "_parameter_filter_path_cache", None)
+    cache_lock = getattr(workspace_obj, "_parameter_filter_path_cache_lock", None)
+
+    # Fall back to direct resolution when a cache is unavailable (e.g. lightweight callers).
+    if not isinstance(cache, dict):
+        return process_input_path(workspace_obj.repository_directory, file_path_filter)
+
+    # Build a hashable cache key from the filter (None, str, or list of str).
+    cache_key = tuple(file_path_filter) if isinstance(file_path_filter, list) else file_path_filter
+
+    if cache_lock is not None:
+        with cache_lock:
+            if cache_key in cache:
+                return cache[cache_key]
+
+    # Resolve outside the lock so concurrent threads resolving different filters don't serialize.
+    resolved = process_input_path(workspace_obj.repository_directory, file_path_filter)
+
+    if cache_lock is not None:
+        with cache_lock:
+            cache.setdefault(cache_key, resolved)
+            return cache[cache_key]
+
+    cache[cache_key] = resolved
+    return resolved
+
+
 def process_environment_key(environment: str, replace_value_dict: dict) -> dict:
     """Processes the replace_value dictionary to replace the '_ALL_' environment key with the target environment when present."""
     # If there's only one key, check if it's "_ALL_" (case insensitive) and replace it

@@ -633,6 +633,148 @@ def test_extract_parameter_filters(self, mock_workspace):
             assert item_name is None
